subject: [PATCH v1] mm: unqueue deferred split folios outside the lruvec lock

reviews.author: Lance Yang
reviews.summary: Reviewer Lance Yang asked for measurement data to assess whether unqueueing deferred split folios outside the lruvec lock results in measurable overhead and requested before/after numbers on this change
reviews.raw_body:
Nice work! Thanks!

BTW, have you seen measurable overhead from unqueueing deferred split
folios under the lruvec lock?

Any before/after numbers for this change, including the cost of the extra
pass over the batch?

Cheers, Lance

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) questioned the wording in an existing comment, suggesting a more accurate description of dequeuing large folios instead of 'part of a huge page'.
reviews.raw_body:
In general, this lgtm, thanks. I am confused about this existing comment you are
moving.

folios being *part of* a huge page? Huh? A folio might represent a huge page,
but what does the "part of" thing mean here.

Is it simply "Dequeue any large folios" ?

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the swapoff path needs to drop the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(), agreed to restructure in v2.

Author agreed that unqueuing deferred split folios is necessary for large folios, and promised to reword the comment in v2.
reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, Oct 14, 2026 at 2:31 AM David Hildenbrand (Arm)
<david@kernel.org> wrote:

---

Agreed, I'll reword this to "Unqueue any large folios from the
deferred split queue to avoid a dangling list entry once the folios
are freed".

Thanks,
Joanne

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges a fix is needed for the performance issue, promises to include benchmark results in the next version of the patch.
reviews.raw_body:

2026-10-14.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel to unqueue deferred split folios outside of the lruvec lock, which is held during certain memory management operations. The change introduces a new function, folio_batch_unqueue_deferred_split(), that can be used in these paths to release the folios from the deferred split queue after the lruvec lock has been released but before they are uncharged. This helps reduce contention and shortens critical sections with IRQs disabled.

2026-10-13.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel to unqueue deferred split folios outside of the lruvec lock, which is held during certain memory management operations. The change introduces a new function, folio_batch_unqueue_deferred_split(), that can be used in these paths to release the folios from the deferred split queue after the lruvec lock has been released but before they are uncharged. This helps reduce contention and shortens critical sections with IRQs disabled.
